findings.title: Rival responses carried through the pericope
findings.claim: The disagreement in 32:25 can also be heard as a contest between orientations carried through a community: turning away and uncertainty stand beside leaders who guide by command after patience and certainty. The focus remains a judgment over matters on which people disagree.
findings.mechanism: The focus verb yakhtalifuna carries the accepted KHLF branch for distinct paths and disagreement; 32:22-23 and 32:24 provide the concrete contrast. The succession facet adds a bounded possibility of continuity through the leaders and those who follow them, so the dispute gains a social, transmissible dimension.
findings.reader_payoff: The dispute is newly perceptible as a contrast between responses to guidance, not only as a set of opposing propositions.
findings.containment: The Form VIII focus verb still says that they disagree. Succession is a contextual root resonance, not a claim that yakhtalifuna itself means replacing a predecessor; the packet does not identify a specific office transfer or a complete historical chain. Adjacent examples without a transmission relation remain a possible reading.

findings.reader_payoff: The promised judgment can be perceived as concerning historically linked communities whose outcomes remain readable in the places later people inhabit.
findings.containment: The immediate reading still concerns the parties who differ. The packet does not identify the past cohorts' precise disputes or say that every cohort held the same position; the cross-generational extension remains an attributed inference.

findings.reader_payoff: The promise of judgment is newly legible as an answer to the demand for an opening whose arrival ends the possibility of waiting it out.
findings.containment: The judicial meaning of yafsilu remains primary. Fath can also carry a victory nuance, which the source leaves live; this reading does not decide between those nuances or assert a schedule beyond the supplied verses.

findings.title: The adjudicating Lord is also the sustainer
findings.claim: The pericope lets Rabbuka carry the nurturing force of its root: later in the same sequence, water is driven to barren land and growth is brought out. The promised judge is thus heard beside the sustaining work the text has shown.
findings.mechanism: The focus's accepted RBB branch describes tending something toward completion; the independent water-to-growth scene in 32:27 triggers that branch. The title Rabb meets the divine act of bringing life from dry land, so judgment and provision belong to one portrayal of the Lord.
findings.reader_payoff: The adjudicator is not an abstract authority: the pericope has also shown the sustaining work associated with the title.
findings.containment: Rabb remains the title of Lord and the ruling remains judicial. The crop scene illustrates a root resonance; it does not make Rabb mean agriculture or turn judgment into a harvest metaphor.

epistemic.reason: The focus branch is accepted and the exact 32:27 surface is supplied. The context word-root coordinates come through a legacy_unbound HFT trace, so the contact is kept local and qualified.
